tables.label: Table 1
tables.caption: Twelve clinical Salmonella isolates used for antibacterial and antibiofilm assays in this study.
footnotes: CSF: cerebrospinal fluid. AMP: ampicillin. SXT: trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole. KZ: cephazolin. CN: gentamicin. TE: tetracycline. NA: nalidixic acid. C: chloramphenicol. TZP: piperacillin/tazobactam. CIP: ciprofloxacin.

tables.label: Table 2
tables.caption: Physicochemical properties of peptides and variants designed in this study.
footnotes: MW: molecular weight. pI: isoelectric point. z: net charge. HR: hydrophobic ratio. ACN: acetonitrile. µH: hydrophobic moment. nd: no data/not determined. h: α-helix. c: random coil. e: extended strand. ?: ambiguous states. Italic letters indicate redesigned peptides in this study. Lowercase amino acids indicate d-form amino acids. C-terminal amidation is presented by -NH2. * MW determined using MALDI-TOF MS, mass spectra shown in Figure S1.

tables.label: Table 3
tables.caption: Antibacterial activity of the variant peptides shown as MIC (MBC) in µM tested against 12 clinical Salmonella isolates.
footnotes: MIC: minimal inhibitory concentration. MBC: minimal bactericidal concentration. GM: geometric mean.

tables.label: Table 4
tables.caption: Hemolytic activity of the variant peptides on sheep red blood cells shown in percent hemolysis and their SI toward Salmonella.
footnotes: HC50: hemolytic concentration 50. SI: selectivity index. * Hemolysis (%) at its MIC value(s).
